newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes extend fall with NYMEX softer.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes extend fall with NYMEX softer.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices fell in late trading on Thursday, tracking weakness in November spot West Texas Intermediate, which was curbed by profit-taking in futures markets.

Traders said local trade was "dead" with an impasse looming for Alaska North Slope crude as sellers last offered at $2.15 off October WTI. Buyers priced the market at $2.50 under November, which ended 50 cents under October's levels on Wednesday.
Outright prices for ANS were $21.60/21.90 a barrel against $21.90/22.20 on Wednesday.
Line 63 remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
California heavy crude Kern River were unchanged at $16.15/16.35 a barrel.
Prices for lightly traded Wilmington crude oil held at $17.60/17.70.
